business_interpretation: The decline is real and reconciles to the cent across Phases 4 to 7.
permitted_conclusion: Net revenue fell by this amount in the week-aligned H2 comparison.
not_permitted_conclusion: Any statement of why it fell, from this number alone.
recommended_next_step: Use it as the fixed baseline for every later review.

finding: Attribution: cluster -€397,778, stock-outs -€37,235, 'Faulty' returns -€31,589, Home & Kitchen -€186,146, residual -€78,522; total -€731,270.50
business_interpretation: An exclusive split of the decline into estimated components plus a remainder.
permitted_conclusion: Each component is an estimate of how much of the change sits with that driver, without double counting.
not_permitted_conclusion: Adding other estimates (for example the other promotion methods or the stock-out upper bound) to it; reading a component as proof of its cause.
recommended_next_step: Quote components with their evidence level every time.

finding: S03 to S05 transactions per store -27.8% vs -1.1% in matched controls; step change on 15 Jul 2025
business_interpretation: A sudden loss of receipts specific to three stores, still present at the end of the data.
permitted_conclusion: Three stores lost receipts relative to comparable stores from mid-July 2025; the excess decline is estimated at -€397,778.
not_permitted_conclusion: That footfall fell (there is no footfall data); that a competitor, local event, staffing or customer behaviour caused it.
recommended_next_step: Investigate in stages: data completeness, store operations, footfall and conversion, local environment, customers (A01 to A04).

finding: External or local cause of the cluster loss
business_interpretation: The pattern fits an outside cause, but an unrecorded internal change fits equally.
permitted_conclusion: An external or unrecorded operational cause is a hypothesis consistent with the data.
not_permitted_conclusion: Naming any cause, or acting as if one were known.
recommended_next_step: Collect DR01 to DR11; hold targeted spend (A06).

finding: Full-week stock-outs in Electronics & Tech rose from 0 to 786; no sales in those weeks
business_interpretation: Root-cause evidence for lost sales during observed full-week stock-outs.
permitted_conclusion: Full-week stock-outs caused lost sales, estimated at €37,235 gross, €23,963 net of deferred demand.
not_permitted_conclusion: That the supplier failed; that fixing availability will return €37,235 (it is a historical estimate, not a forecast).
recommended_next_step: Low-risk replenishment controls now (A07, A08); investigate supply vs ordering (A10).

finding: Voltix SKUs hold 83% of the lost sales; their stock-out rate rose 6.8 pp more than other suppliers'
evidence_level: STATISTICAL ASSOCIATION; Phase 6 D04: Statistical association
business_interpretation: Stock-out concentration is associated with Voltix SKUs. Available data cannot determine whether the cause was supplier performance or Brightwater ordering/replenishment.
permitted_conclusion: Stock-out concentration is associated with Voltix SKUs.
not_permitted_conclusion: Supplier failure, without purchase order and ASN evidence; that Brightwater's ordering was at fault, equally.
recommended_next_step: Order-to-receipt review (A10); no supplier sanction until then (A12).

finding: Electronics 'Faulty' refunds up €31,589 (+90%), concentrated in S13, S14, S07, S15, S16 and in items sold from September 2025
business_interpretation: An observed change in a recorded till reason.
permitted_conclusion: More Electronics refunds were recorded as 'Faulty', mainly in five stores and recent sale months.
not_permitted_conclusion: That the products are defective; that a supplier shipped a bad batch.
recommended_next_step: Hold returns for inspection with batch capture (A13); audit recording practice (A14).

finding: Product defect vs recording practice behind 'Faulty' returns
business_interpretation: Either explanation fits; no QA data either way.
permitted_conclusion: A product-quality problem and a recording change are both hypotheses.
not_permitted_conclusion: Choosing one without inspection, batch or RMA evidence.

finding: Home & Kitchen discount rate 2.4% to 11.9%; events 2,427 to 8,848
business_interpretation: The promotion programme became much deeper and more frequent.
permitted_conclusion: Promotion depth and frequency rose sharply.
not_permitted_conclusion: That this rise was a mistake or a success, from the rise alone.

finding: Home & Kitchen promotion effect: M1 -€186,146, M4 -€265,003, M2 +€97,505, M3 +€79,059
business_interpretation: Promotion activity is associated with the Home & Kitchen decline, but causality is not established. The methods disagree in sign.
permitted_conclusion: Promotion activity is associated with the Home & Kitchen decline.
not_permitted_conclusion: That promotions caused the category decline; summing or averaging the four methods into one promotion impact.
recommended_next_step: Controlled depth test (A20); no blanket change meanwhile (A21).

finding: Outside the cluster, continuing Electronics SKUs -€294,304; new SKUs +€265,233; delisted -€95,472
business_interpretation: A partition of the change; the decline sits in continuing SKUs.
permitted_conclusion: Continuing SKUs sold less per ranged week while new SKUs added revenue.
not_permitted_conclusion: That customers switched to new models (a hypothesis); delisting continuing SKUs on this evidence.
recommended_next_step: Monthly range split with range-plan dates (A23).

evidence_level: NOT ATTRIBUTED; Phase 6 D09: Observed change
business_interpretation: Part of the decline has no identified driver; it also carries the uncertainty of the estimates.
not_permitted_conclusion: Assigning it to any driver to make the explanation complete.

finding: Scenario values for stock-outs (see the impact framework)
business_interpretation: Restatements of the H2 2025 estimate under stated assumptions.
permitted_conclusion: Under the stated assumptions, about this much of the H2 2025 loss would have been avoided.
not_permitted_conclusion: A forecast, a target or a promised recovery.
recommended_next_step: Measure the effect of the controls instead (61 to 90 days).
